text:
Sam H: hey folks — ran into a customer case where streaming responses count partial tokens twice on reconnects, causing them to blow burst quotas
Jana L: ugh, seen that. is it double-counting because the client resends the last chunk or because we don't reconcile resumed stream offset?
Sam H: looks like both. client resends fragments after reconnect, and our per-key accounting treats each packet as new tokens because session-id changed
Mike T: can we use a resume id + token-offset map in the quota service to dedupe? store small (resume_id -> last_counted_offset) for short TTL
Rahul P: that's the idea. but concern: per-key memory explosion if every client opens many streams. need eviction policy and strict TTL
Jana L: agreed. what about per-org vs per-key enforcement? customer wants org-wide fairness so one key doesn't eat bursts for everyone
Sam H: product asked for both: per-key hard limit + per-org shared burst pool. question: when reclaiming credits on reconnect (if we dedupe), where does the credit refund go? back to key or org pool?
Mike T: refund to the pool that originally provided the credit. if org pool supplied burst to key, refund to org pool. but we need traceability on allocation events
Rahul P: implement allocation records: alloc_id -> {source: org|key, amount, ts}. small, append-only, TTLed to 24h. reconcile job replays allocations to refund if dedupe indicates overcount
Sam H: can we avoid external job by making realtime reconciliation in quota service on stream-resume? if resume_id matches and offsets indicate overlap, atomically decrement counted_tokens and credit back
Jana L: atomic ops across redis counters + allocation log might work. trick is to make it crash-safe. what if quota service crashes mid-refund?
Mike T: use Redis Lua to do compare-and-swap: check resume key -> last_offset, compute overlap, decrement, update last_offset. single atomic script. expiration handles stale entries
Sam H: pseudo: 
```
-- keys: resume:<resume_id>, quota:<key_id>
local last = redis.call('GET', KEYS[1]) or 0
if tonumber(ARGV[1]) <= tonumber(last) then
  return 0 -- nothing new
end
local overlap = math.max(0, tonumber(last) - tonumber(ARGV[2]))
if overlap > 0 then
  redis.call('DECRBY', KEYS[2], overlap)
end
redis.call('SET', KEYS[1], ARGV[1], 'EX', 300)
return overlap
```
Mike T: rough but shows the pattern
Rahul P: care: DECRBY on quota counter might put negative values. we must bound at zero and reflect reclaimed tokens back into burst pool counters too
Jana L: UX question: Console should surface per-stream resume events and reclaimed credits so support sees why a spike happened. add a 'streaming resume' timeline for top offenders
Sam H: +1. Also expose a metric streaming.partial_token_dedupe and streaming.resume_reclaimed_tokens for alerting
ops-bot: deployment scheduled for quota-service v2 at 2026-04-01 03:00 UTC :rocket:
Sam H: also need to decide retention on resume ids. 5 minutes? 10? customer uses flaky mobile networks, often reconnects within 2-3 mins
Mike T: I vote 10m TTL default, configurable per-org. longer TTL increases state but reduces false double-billing
Rahul P: add rate for keys with many concurrent streams: cap stored resume entries per key to e.g., 100, fallback to no-dedupe when exceeded and emit metric
Jana L: sounds good. final API change: resume token sent as header `X-Resume-Id` and body includes resumed_offset. server returns `resume-accepted` with overlap count
Sam H: compatibility: old clients without resume id will keep working (no dedupe). document in API changelog and add a rollout plan: opt-in header then enforce after 2 weeks
Mike T: PR incoming for redis lua + unit tests. I'll add metrics + console panel wiring.
Sam H: thanks. anyone object to storing allocation records for 24h and using Lua-based realtime reclaim on resume?
Rahul P: no objections from me. let's keep limits conservative and monitor for edge cases
Jana L: ok — I'll draft a short support playbook and console mock for the timeline
Sam H: great. moving to implement. :thumbsup:
